name: Jarrell Plantation farmhouse

location.text: 711 Jarrell Plantation Road, Juliette, Jones County, Georgia

dates.note: Wikipedia infobox 'Built 1847, 1895, 1920' for the site as a whole; the 1847 house is John Fitz Jarrell's, the 1895 house his son Benjamin Richard Jarrell's, as the node's exemplar says. The Digital Library of Georgia: 'In 1847, John Fitz Jarrell built a simple heart-pine house typical of most plantations'.

refs.title: NRHP reference No. 73000624; added May 9, 1973 (as the Wikipedia infobox prints it)
refs.note: Read from the infobox as the search result printed it, not from the National Register's own database. The infobox locates it at '711 Jarrell Plantation Road, East Juliette, Georgia'.

refs.title: Jarrell Plantation State Historic Site - Digital Library of Georgia
refs.note: A state parks brochure held by the Digital Library of Georgia; it carries the 1847 heart-pine statement.

refs.title: Jarrell Plantation Historic Site | Friends of Georgia State Parks
refs.note: 'this cotton plantation was owned by a single family for more than 140 years'.

note: The register lists the whole site as a district; the exemplar names the 1847 house within it, so this record's dates are the house's and its numbers are the site's. No HABS survey was sought beyond the register query; none appeared. Seeded 4 Sep 2026.
